title: Why Does Time FLY as You Get Older? ⏳
description:
You blow out your candles... and somehow it's already your birthday again.

The leading idea: looking back, your brain judges how long a stretch of time was by how many new memories it left. As a kid almost everything is a first, so one summer leaves a mountain of them. As an adult the days repeat, far less gets saved, and the whole year looks short in hindsight. It is a leading explanation, not a settled one: in surveys it is mostly the last ten years that feel faster with age, and feeling rushed plays a part too. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

The tower is real. In 2007, scientists dropped volunteers about 30 metres into a net. Asked afterwards, they judged their own fall to have lasted 36% longer than the same fall watched from the ground... even though a flickering display strapped to their wrists showed they were not actually seeing in slow motion. A small study, but a neat one: richer memories make time look longer. So do something new this week.
